results.comment: Hi Simone! I am a 14 year old boy who loves Tesla, EV’s, and a thyroid cancer survivor! My mother basically saved my life (moms are the best ❤️)! My story is below and I encourage everyone to read it. Thank you. ☺️   Okay so around Labor Day weekend I went horseback riding for 3 days had a fun time, came home and went to school the next day. I went to the nurses office for an ice pack because the outside of my neck hurt and not the inside. I told my mom what went on at school and told her I went to the nurses office, she said “I want you to take a drink of water then tilt your head up to the ceiling.” I was confused why she was telling me but I did it anyways. She saw my thyroid (it’s shaped like a butterfly in your throat) moving up and down. She told me we are going to the doctor right now (and again really confused me didn’t know what the hell was going on). We went to the doctors office at about 8:00 PM and my mom explained what was happening. The doctor then tells me I’m getting a ultrasound on my neck where my thyroid is. I was scared at first thinking they had to stick something inside my throat, all it is is pretty much putting this warm gel on the camera and moving it to see other parts. It was very relaxing I must say. Anyways, the doctor called my parents and recommended that they take me to a ENT (ears, nose, throat) and have him check something’s out with my neck. Now it’s about the 3rd week in November and I had my second ultrasound to see if anything changed, sadly nothing did 😞. My ENT said let’s preform a biopsy (to see if it was cancerous or not). Now I was really worried, because I’ve never been under anesthesia before and I’ve never been in a real hospital before. My ENT did the operation and when he was done he left the room and pulled my parents aside and told them that things aren’t looking to pretty… and he said “Where would you like to go for treatment I can’t do much more for your son.” I didn’t know that was going on, couple days later the news got out and I had Papillary Thyroid Cancer. My mother was in tears and I hugged her for a very long time, I wasn’t crying at all.  On 1/5/18 I arrived at the University of Chicago children’s hospital and I was operated for 12 HOURS (1 hour for pre operation, 1 for post operation, and 10 for surgery)! I sadly got the flu and had to stay a WHOLE week. My whole thyroid was removed along with 36 other lymph nodes that were affected by the cancer. I was left with a huge scar from ear-to-ear and 2 drain scars (drainage from my collarbone). I had great nurses who made my day better and one nurse called me a badass! I felt so good after hearing that and made a poem about myself going through thyroid cancer! It’s about the end of the last week in January and it’s about to start February. My endocrinologist said that I have to start this low iodine diet and starve my body from iodine, I had no choice but to do it and start radioactive iodine for treatment. I was back at the University of Chicago Comers Children’s hospital again and spent the night there for my treatment. I had breakfast took a shower, couple hours later I was throwing up my life. I was pressing every single nurse or help button there was in my room and finally got a nurse to come into my room to help me. I was done throwing up, couple hours after that I became really really dizzy to the point where I passed out on my bed, I heard very high pitched noises while I was dizzy and again pressed every single help button, another nurse came to help me and took my radioactivity level, she said that I could go home and get into my room for isolation. I was so so so bored out of my mind in my own room! I even got tired of playing on my phone (shocking to me because I’m literally attached to my phone). Last day of isolation my dad was making homemade pizza, I asked for extra cheese (I couldn’t have any dairy on my low iodine diet) and I was in HEAVEN! I felt normal again after eating cheese for the first time in forever! (😂)  I have remained cancer free for 1 year and my diagnosis date is coming up soon on 12/11/2019, hopefully making that 2 years cancer free.  If you are ever going through a hard time in life, don’t worry! You will get through this! Remain positive and your family and friends always will have your back!
